intent: The user wanted the BGH’s requirements for explaining an Eigenbedarfskündigung under § 573 Abs. 2 Nr. 2 BGB, particularly what the termination notice must say.

claims.claim: Under § 573 Abs. 3 BGB, the notice must identify the reason for termination; for Eigenbedarf, the BGH generally considers it sufficient to name the person who needs the dwelling and explain that person’s interest in obtaining it.
claims.note: The BGH states this general standard in VIII ZR 167/17, consistent with VIII ZR 317/10.

claims.claim: The notice should practically include the beneficiary’s prior housing situation, why this particular dwelling is needed, detailed information about a work move, and why alternative dwellings are unsuitable.
claims.note: This presents too many details as practical requirements. In VIII ZR 317/10, the BGH said the prior housing situation did not need to be stated in the circumstances of that case, and that the formal requirement is not a demand for detailed advance proof. The BGH’s later formulation likewise says the notice generally need only identify the beneficiary and explain their interest.

claims.claim: The BGH’s 24 September 2025 decision, VIII ZR 289/23, concerned a landlord planning to alter and sell his own dwelling and use the rented dwelling; the BGH set aside the appellate decision and remanded the case.
claims.note: This is a material Eigenbedarf ruling, not a new formal notice requirement.

notes: The answer gives the central BGH standard correctly, but its practical checklist overstates what must generally appear in the notice. The 2025 decision is accurately described, though it concerns the substantive Eigenbedarf assessment rather than the formal explanation requirement. Arithmetic: Answers 25/30 + Accuracy (50 − 10 for one contradicted supporting claim) + Freshness 10/10 + Calibration 7/10 = 82/100.

claims.claim: The regular deadline is the end of the second calendar year after the contribution year; therefore, the deadline for 2024 is 31 December 2026.

claims.claim: With a Dauerzulageantrag, the provider applies for the allowance each year, so the saver does not need to submit a new annual application; the authorization can be revoked by the end of the relevant contribution year.

claims.note: The ZfA identifies the Kinderergänzungsbogen as the form for claiming child allowance and says providers provide the necessary forms when circumstances change.

claims.claim: The Kinderzulage is €300 for a child born after 31 December 2007 and €185 for an older child.
claims.note: These amounts and the birth-date distinction appear in §85 EStG.

claims.claim: Once the application deadline expires, the allowance for that year is definitively lost.
claims.note: The general deadline is an exclusion period, but §90(2) provides an exception for certain child-rearing eligible persons and their eligible spouses. The answer states the general rule too absolutely.

intent: The user is seeking the legal distinction between a correction under § 153 AO and a voluntary disclosure under § 371 AO, specifically how intent at the time of the original tax filing affects which applies.

claims.claim: The answer presents the dividing line as a strict choice: if the original filing was intentional, § 153 AO no longer applies and only § 371 AO can provide relief.
claims.note: The BMF’s AEAO to § 153, consistent with the BGH decision, says a § 153 reporting and correction duty can also exist when the taxpayer initially acted with conditional intent but only later reaches certain knowledge that the statement was wrong. The answer mentions this later, but its categorical table and statement that § 153 is not applicable with intent conflict with that qualification.

claims.claim: For reckless tax understatement, correction under § 378(3) AO can prevent a fine if made before notice of proceedings; if tax was already underpaid, the tax must also be paid within the allowed period.
claims.note: This accurately summarizes § 378(3) AO.

claims.claim: A voluntary disclosure under § 371 AO requires complete correction and has blocking grounds; § 398a surcharges are among its requirements.
claims.note: Completeness, blocking grounds, and payment requirements are supported. But § 398a is not a general surcharge requirement for every § 371 disclosure: it applies in specified cases where immunity fails only because of the amount or a particularly serious case. See https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ao_1977/__398a.html.

claims.claim: Failure to correct after the relevant later recognition can constitute tax evasion by omission; the BGH held that the correction duty may apply after an initially conditional-intent filing.

claims.claim: An internal tax-control system may be evidence against intent or recklessness, but does not replace examination of the individual case.

intent: The user is checking the current meaning and status of the 20-person threshold for appointing a data protection officer under § 38 BDSG.

claims.claim: As of October 20, 2026, § 38(1) BDSG still requires a data protection officer when an organization regularly employs at least 20 people constantly engaged in automated processing of personal data; the provision also contains appointment duties independent of headcount in specified cases.
claims.note: The current official statutory text states the 20-person threshold and the separate duties for processing subject to a DPIA or certain commercial data-processing purposes.

claims.claim: The threshold was raised from 10 to 20 in 2019 by the 2. DSAnpUG-EU.
claims.note: The 2019 amendment is published in the Federal Law Gazette; the current official law contains the 20-person wording.

claims.claim: The Dresdner Institut für Datenschutz says that, in general, having an email account at work is enough to count as automated processing for the threshold.
claims.note: The cited institute states this interpretation. It should be understood as that institute’s guidance, not as a rule written expressly into the statute; the Bavarian supervisory authority, for example, says mere access to a member list alone does not make everyone count.

claims.claim: The Föderale Modernisierungsagenda adopted on December 4, 2025 says the federal government will introduce a repeal of § 38(1) BDSG by December 31, 2026, limiting the non-public-sector appointment duty to Article 37 GDPR.
claims.note: The agenda’s item 160 gives that deadline and proposed action. It announces a planned bill, not a repeal already in force; the current § 38 text remains operative.

claims.claim: The 20-person threshold was not replaced by a 50-person threshold on January 1, 2025.
claims.note: The current official text still sets the threshold at 20. The answer also appropriately describes the 50-person idea as a proposal rather than enacted law.

notes: The answer directly supplies the threshold and correctly distinguishes the current law from a future reform proposal. Arithmetic: query 30/30 + accuracy 50/50 (no checked claims contradicted) + freshness 10/10 + calibration 10/10 = 100/100. The email-access point is properly attributed to DIDS, though readers should treat it as an interpretive position rather than statutory wording.
